summary: SIEM feed s180_triple is degraded: 15.3% of frames are dropped as oversize (>1518B, up to 8108B), 28.3% arrive still ERSPAN-encapsulated and opaque to the SIEM, and 19.4% are duplicates wasting capacity.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo frames and ERSPAN-encapsulated frames up to 8108 bytes to a 1 Gbps SIEM port with 1518-byte MTU. ERSPAN overhead pushes frames over the NIC limit so the card drops them before the SIEM can process them.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM silently drops 581 of 3808 frames (15.3%) at the NIC, creating a blind spot - those flows/events are never parsed, correlated or alerted.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM has needs_full_payload=false and needs only headers/metadata, so slicing/trimming to 1518B at the broker preserves detection value while preventing NIC drops. If full payload is later required, use mtu_advice to raise SIEM MTU or lower network MTU instead.

findings.root_cause: 1076 of 3808 frames (28.3%) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel. Broker is mirroring/ERSPAN-forwarding without stripping the outer tunnel header before delivery to the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM without ERSPAN decapsulation cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP headers or payload, so 28.3% of traffic is opaque to detection and correlation rules, reducing coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Strip ERSPAN at the packet broker to present native inner packets to the SIEM, restoring visibility without requiring tool-side tunnel support.

findings.root_cause: 19.4% duplicates (737 of 3808) from overlapping SPAN/ERSPAN sources or aggregation of same traffic via multiple broker ingress ports without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: Wastes SIEM 1G ingest, license and storage on redundant packets, inflates counts and can skew correlation/analytics while leaving less headroom for unique traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (window-based) to drop identical packets before delivery, freeing bandwidth for unique events.
